summary: Cecil County, MD 100-ft steel tower begun January 1935 under state forestry supervision; staffed by Harry Hartenstine into 1944; FFLA lists it standing, condition and access unverified.

facts.design: 100-foot steel fire tower with a cab
facts.agency: Maryland state forestry (District Forest Warden and District Forester supervised construction)

events.note: Construction began January 2, 1935 under District Forest Warden Charles W. Bayles; site bought from local owners for $50
Harry Hartenstine, who had run the Foys Hill tower for more than ten years, took up duties at Woodlawn
First smoke reported April 3, 1935 proved to be a field being burned off by its owners
Tower equipped with two-way radio; Hartenstine still operating it

notes_for_editor: Construction and staffing facts come from two 1935 and one 1944 Midland Journal item reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page; the reprint ends in 1944. Current status rests only on the FFLA list. The Cecil County History blog (cecilcountyhistory.com, post on fire towers) reportedly says the tower still stands, has a 2011 photo, and that the state stopped operating the towers, with seasonal staffing into the 1970s. fetch_text got HTTP 403 for that page, so it is not cited and needs checking. A DNR poster reportedly says Aeromotor built most Maryland towers; no source read names Woodlawn's builder, so none is stated. The brief record had no agency; the agency fact is worded from the District Forest Warden quote. No licensed photo found, so none added. Access level left unset: no source described access.
